html:
Isaac Newton was an English mathematician and physicist whose laws of motion and universal gravitation, published in 1687, showed that the same simple laws govern a falling apple and the orbits of the planets. His work crowned the Scientific Revolution.

He was born in Lincolnshire in 1643 (Christmas Day 1642 in the old Julian calendar England still used). He studied at Cambridge, and in 1665 to 1666, when plague closed the university, he worked at home on calculus, light and gravity.

His main work:

  • Principia (1687): three laws of motion and the law of gravity, which explained Kepler's planetary orbits, the tides and the paths of comets.
  • Calculus, worked out at the same time as Leibniz, which led to a bitter dispute over who came first.
  • Optics: he showed that white light is a mix of colours and built the first practical reflecting telescope.

He built on Copernicus and Galileo, and his physics replaced the system of Aristotle that had stood for two thousand years. He also spent years on alchemy and on reading Bible prophecy, which he kept largely private.

Later he ran the Royal Mint in London, chasing forgers and reforming the coinage, and was president of the Royal Society from 1703. He was knighted in 1705. Enlightenment writers such as Voltaire made him a hero of reason, and his mechanics stood unchallenged until Einstein.
